decisions.reason: F5 omitted local path connectivity and semilocal simple connectivity, but the actual Y is a connected manifold with contractible ball or half-ball charts; thus the application was valid. Qualified F5 and verified these hypotheses in step 3.1. Mayer-Vietoris gives meridian-generated Z homology in degree one, the connected double-cover transfer is an H1 isomorphism over F2, and the branched attachment kills it. Compact CW domination and UCT imply rational acyclicity. Statement unchanged.

The rejection is fatal logic: for N=[0,1], M=R3, C={1/2}, f(t)=(t(t-1/2),0,0), df(1/2) is nonzero and the boundary images are distinct, but f(0)=f(1/2); any map fixed on both sets is noninjective. Separated the relative and boundary-only results; simultaneous fixing uses the relative embedding hypothesis on C union boundary N. The finite bump families span jets and separated-point values, bad ranks have codimension (m-r)(n-r)>n, and the diagonal has codimension m>2n. Compact local and separated-pair estimates preserve embedding on D1. Added exact collar and countable-null-union uses; arbitrary C1 approximation, closed-set relative embedding and boundary-only embedding remain proved under countable choice.
